title: Tier routing T2 howto
desc: T2 domain tier of claude-code-agent-tier-routing. Briefing recipes, dispatcher syntax, conductor pattern (Opus/Sonnet recursive), fan-out execution rules. Consult when writing a brief or dispatching a conductor.
steps: NAV: T2 domain tier of claude-code-agent-tier-routing. Briefing recipes, dispatcher syntax, conductor patterns, fan-out execution. Core decision rules and WillKim standing orders in T1 (wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing). Constitution preamble, glossary, history, samjil-prevention lessons in T3 (wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing-ref).

BRIEFING QUALITY IS EVERYTHING (2026-05-16): Agent capability matters less than brief quality. Haiku and Codex-mini follow precise instructions well -- they fail when the brief is vague. HAIKU: write step-by-step run X, check Y, do Z commands. No open-ended tasks. No judgment calls. Verify each action has one observable output. CODEX-MINI: write imperative DO steps with absolute paths + one exit criterion (e.g. verify git diff --stat shows N files changed). Codex stops when it thinks done -- vague goals = early exit. BOTH: do what makes sense is not a valid instruction. Run wkappbot skill read X, then if output contains Y do Z, else do W is valid. Precision in = precision out.

BRIEFING UNIVERSAL RULE: Precision in = precision out, for ALL agent tiers. Simple, clear, precise briefs beat vague open-ended ones regardless of model. Step-by-step run X, check Y, do Z with one observable output per step. HAIKU/CODEX-MINI: add absolute paths + self-verifiable exit criterion. OPUS/TRIAD: precise steps save their judgment budget for hard decisions, not for interpreting vague prompts.

CODEX IS DEFAULT EXECUTION AGENT (2026-05-15 mandatory): For any mechanical file edit, refactor, multi-file work, or implementation task -- reach for Codex FIRST, before Opus. Codex-mini is significantly cheaper and faster than Opus for hands-on execution. Opus is for judgment, architecture, and stuck bugs only. Pattern: codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -C cwd then wkappbot skill read A, B, C and the task. Windows sandbox fix: --dangerously-bypass is REQUIRED (-s workspace-write fails with spawn setup refresh). Use wkcodex.ps1 wrapper: powershell -File wkcodex.ps1 with skill reads + task. wkcodex auto-injects bypass, enforces 3 skill refs, runs post-checks (git diff, CP949). Hooks not supported in codex exec mode (only TUI). Session: codex resume --last to continue, codex fork --last to branch. Always verify rc=0 -- codex may report success while underlying op failed silently.

CODEX ROUTING (updated 2026-05-26): source splits/refactors -> wkcodex task (preferred over codex exec direct). wkcodex wrapper sets sandbox+model automatically. codex resume/fork/apply still direct. The dispatcher cmd is secondary option when wkcodex unavailable.

DELEGATION POLICY (user 2026-05-30, harness-enforced). ONE skill = no per-agent doc drift. TIER LADDER: Opus = judgment/orchestration/user-spokesperson (NEVER delegate the representation -- mail-review/legal/schedule judgment stays with Opus); Sonnet = default work AND can CONDUCT a detail sub-project (impl -> test -> delegate landing); Haiku = survey/reads/QA-canary; Codex(codex-mini) = code/refactor/source-review; triad/gpt = hard/ambiguous/design. SAME-TIER BLOCK (live guard): X->X is pure overhead and is BLOCKED -- always CHANGE tier. CHEAP-COMMIT RULE: cheap models are blocked by pre-commit source-gate; after they implement + selftest-green, they hand the COMMIT to Opus via the dispatcher cmd --model opus with 5-pt SPEC + 3 wkappbot skill read refs. CONDUCTOR PATTERN: Opus may hand leadership of a bounded detail sub-project to Sonnet; Sonnet then orchestrates cheaper tiers under same rules. BUDGET: Opus is priciest -- prefer talk(judgment)+delegate over solo tool-grinding; stall-guard (Opus 7min) + same-tier block enforce. STALL: time-only per tier (Opus 7 / Sonnet 6 / Haiku 3 min), resets on any successful delegation.

OPUS MISSION (user 2026-05-30): keep cheaper tiers WORKING -- even when Opus has nothing to execute itself, its job is to keep Sonnet/Haiku/Codex busy via delegation. Idling without delegating is a failure; Opuss value = CONTINUOUS orchestration + judgment, never solo grinding. Practical loop while resting: queue/hand the next bounded sub-task to a cheap conductor (Sonnet leads detail sub-projects; Haiku surveys/QA; Codex codes), then review + land. COROLLARY: invest in wkappbot(wk-tool) EXECUTION SPEED -- faster wk-tools mean less wall-clock waiting on each call, which buys Opus more conducting headroom under weekly budget. Treat slow wk-tool paths as worth optimizing.

SONNET-AS-CONDUCTOR (user 2026-05-30): recursive conductor ladder applies to Sonnet too. When Sonnet leads a sub-project it MUST delegate grunt work DOWN to preserve its own conducting headroom: surveys/reads/QA -> Haiku (dispatcher cmd --model haiku), code/refactor/source-review -> Codex (dispatcher cmd --model codex), and hand source COMMITS up to Opus (cheap can not commit source). Sonnet reserves its own turns for orchestration + judgment, not solo grinding. This playbook is for CONDUCTOR tiers (Opus/Sonnet) -- Haiku/Codex are executors. ENABLEMENT: any Sonnet-conductor brief MUST include wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing in its mandatory skill refs so the conductor actually knows this ladder.

CONDUCTOR SELF-INVESTMENT HINT (user 2026-05-30): a conductor can BUY future conducting time by delegating wkappbot(wk-tool) TOOL SPEED-OPTIMIZATION as a task. When a wk-tool path is repeatedly slow (long wall-clock per call), do not just endure it -- hand profile + speed up this wk-tool path to Codex (or Sonnet). Faster wk-tools = less wall-clock waiting on every future call across ALL tiers = compounding conducting headroom under weekly budget. Self-reinforcing loop: notice slow tool -> delegate optimization -> tool faster -> more conducting time -> repeat.

OPUS AVAILABILITY + SUPERVISION (user 2026-05-30): Opus MUST (a) dispatch delegations in BACKGROUND/parallel (run_in_background) and keep its own turn FREE to respond to the user immediately -- never block waiting on a sub-agent; (b) stay responsive to every WillKim(user) prompt, including periodic cron monitors, while sub-agents run async; (c) SUPERVISE delegated work -- between user turns, glance at each running agents interim output to confirm it is progressing (not stalled/looping), and course-correct or re-brief if a conductor is off-track. Trust-but-verify: a sub-agents final report states intent, not guaranteed correctness -- Opus reviews before declaring done. Net: Opus is an always-available conductor watching the orchestra, not a worker head-down in one task.

FAN-OUT (user 2026-05-30): when workload is large and decomposable, Opus PARTITIONS it into INDEPENDENT units and dispatches MULTIPLE Sonnet conductors in parallel (each in background), one per chunk; each Sonnet recursively delegates its grunt work to Haiku/Codex. Opus briefs each conductor with its scope + supervises the whole fleet (glance at each interim output, re-brief stragglers), staying responsive to the user. RULES: (1) chunks MUST be independent -- no two agents mutating same files (if must, use isolation worktree); (2) keep concurrency sane (a handful, not dozens); (3) cheap conductors still hand source COMMITS up to Opus, so Opus serializes landing step + reviews each. Net: parallel fan-out for throughput, serialized Opus review/land for safety.

FLEET BASELINE (user 2026-05-30): keep a STANDING fleet of 2-3 Sonnet conductors active on Pending backlog at all times -- even with no urgent item. If fewer than 3 Sonnets active, that is the signal backlog is genuinely empty (or items blocked on user-approval/CDP). Opuss idle state = top up the fleet from SONNET-CONDUCT QUEUE, not sit waiting. Urgent items -> dispatch a Sonnet immediately; otherwise pull one IMPORTANT + one NEGLECTED item and assign one Sonnet each. Keep chunks on DIFFERENT files (independent) so parallel conductors do not clobber; Opus serializes commit-landing + review. Concurrency stays a small handful; cheaper-tier fleet burn is budget-smart vs Opus solo.

CONDUCTOR RULE: The conductor (Sonnet/Opus) never types -- only writes specs and verifies results. Keystrokes belong to Codex/Haiku. The moment your hand reaches for Edit/Write: stop and delegate. A conductor who plays an instrument breaks the orchestra. This is the root of all Sonnet bugs (see sonnet-bug-stop-policy PATTERN 6). Conductor-only session = maximum leverage per token.

SONNET ROLE -- WILLKIM APPOINTMENT (2026-05-31): Sonnet = Planner/Designer. Every design, architecture, or plan Sonnet produces MUST be saved as a skill before delegating execution. Pattern: (1) Sonnet designs -> wkappbot skill contribute --id plan-name. (2) Skill becomes the brief for Haiku/Codex execution. (3) Opus reviews output. Design that lives only in conversation is lost. Skill = the durable artifact. No skill = the plan never happened.

SONNET DUTY 2 -- FAN-OUT (2026-05-31): Decompose every task into smallest independent units and dispatch each to Haiku in parallel. One Haiku per atomic task. Never batch into one Haiku. Example: 5 files to analyze = 5 parallel Haiku agents, not 1 Haiku doing all 5. Speed = parallelism x Haiku cheapness. If work can be split: split it. WillKim standing order.

FAN-OUT SPLIT RULES: (1) Independent = different files, different domains, different repos. These run in parallel. (2) Dependent = B needs A output, same file edit. These run serially. (3) Same file = NEVER two Haiku simultaneously. Use worktree isolation (isolation worktree) if parallel file edits unavoidable. (4) Each Haiku gets a single clear atomic task with one observable exit criterion. Vague tasks = early exit.

FAN-OUT CONSTRAINT -- MULTIPROCESSING CHECK: before splitting a task, verify the target is parallelizable. Tests involving shared state (DB, single file, singleton process, in-memory cache, port binding) = NOT splittable. Check: can two instances run simultaneously without conflict? If state is shared: serial only. If stateless or file-isolated: parallel OK. Always verify first -- wrong split wastes more tokens than serial execution.

COMPLETION PROTOCOL (WillKim 2026-05-31): When any delegation task completes, do NOT report done immediately. Spawn 2 parallel Haiku agents to verify independently, then synthesize both results before final report. Pattern: (1) Haiku-A checks artifact exists + content correct. (2) Haiku-B checks pointers/references/side-effects. (3) Sonnet reads both outputs and gives ONE consolidated pass/fail verdict with specific defects. This catches 'comment changed but code unchanged' class of incomplete fixes. No single-agent verification is sufficient.

PLANNING PROTOCOL (WillKim 2026-05-31): Before finalizing any design skill, Sonnet MUST collect 3 Haiku opinions in parallel. Pattern: spawn 3 Haiku agents with different review angles (e.g. feasibility / risk / missing-steps). Incorporate findings before creating the skill. Benefits: (1) Haiku token usage increases naturally, (2) blind spots caught before Opus spends tokens on a flawed plan, (3) 3 independent angles surface different issues. No design skill is complete without 3 Haiku inputs.

PUSH DISCIPLINE: when multiple parallel agents each commit, only ONE push at the end. Agents commit only -- no git push in agent brief unless it is the LAST agent in the chain. Duplicate pushes waste Opus tokens and create race conditions. Pattern: Agent-A commits, Agent-B commits, then Sonnet runs git push once after both complete.

CODEX BUDGET TIP: wkcodex auto-selects model by Codex budget (under40%=gpt-5.5, 40-70%=gpt-5.4, over70%=gpt-5.4-mini). When Codex budget is tight or after 9pm reset and want to conserve: call wkgpt-mini directly instead of wkcodex. wkgpt-mini always forces gpt-5.4-mini regardless of budget.

CONCRETE APPLICATION (user 2026-07-02): the CONDUCTOR RULE (step 13) applied to the emergency-write-freeze gate -- see emergency-write-freeze-escape-ladder-for-non-pro-new-file-creation skill for the specific recipe: Haiku drafts a probe file + self-tests it, root intelligence (whichever tier is conducting this repo) does the promotion (wkappbot file write --source-file, a copy op) plus independent verification, then makes the merge decision. Do not default to escalating mechanical new-file-creation tasks straight to Opus -- Haiku-drafts/root-merges is the default; Opus is reserved for when Haiku's own probe write ALSO deadlocks (double-deadlock case).

DELEGATE-WELL REFLEX (wire it, 2026-06-22): BEFORE every Agent/Agent.cmd dispatch, run the pre-flight -> wkappbot skill read agent-dispatch-preflight. It is the 5-point dispatch checklist (3 skill-read refs incl agent-on-load; the five LITERAL labels Goal:/Files:/Approach:/Constraints:/Exit:; run_in_background=true for Opus; commit/clean-baseline first; pace). A FAILED dispatch re-sends your ENTIRE context, so one contract-complete brief beats N blocked retries. Also delegate the RIGHT shape: mechanical edits + parse-verify + bug-hunt -> Haiku (great at protos); planning/strategy fan-out that itself drives Haiku to test -> Sonnet; canonical harness/source edits stay ROOT-only (subagents redirect to -proto, ROOT merges). NEVER send a throwaway Reply OK delegation to dodge a guard -- a guard is a signpost to do real work, not an obstacle to bypass.
